"source" is just a variable name. The statement assigns it the result of filtering the array items so only truthy elements remain.

Explanation:
- items.filter(Boolean) is shorthand for items.filter(x => Boolean(x)) (or x => !!x).
- filter keeps elements for which the callback returns a truthy value, so this removes falsy values: false, 0, "", null, undefined, and NaN.
- const source makes source a constant binding to the new array (the original items array is not mutated; the array object referenced by source could still be modified via its methods).

Example:
const items = [0, 1, "", "hello", null, undefined, NaN, false, true];
const source = items.filter(Boolean); // source === [1, "hello", true]
